featured_reviews.review_text:
Midday Meal is a strategic program of the Government of India, and is being implemented by Annamrita Foundation previously known as ISKCON Food Relief Foundation (IFRF) in select schools across the country. The aim of this project is to liberate children from the vicious cycle of Malnourishment and Illiteracy.

It is a not-for-profit, non-religious, non-sectarian public charitable organizations formed on April 23, 2004 and registered under the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950

“Annamrita” literally translated means “Food as Pure as Nectar”.

Annamrita believes in providing children with the right nutrition to support their education. Our program is based on the belief that ‘you are what you eat’. Therefore one nutritious meal prepared with compassion and love, the way a mother would prepare a meal for her child, brings thousands of children to school daily.

Annamrita Foundation serves over 1 million meals every single day, through its 20 kitchens across India. We have a presence in 7 states namely - Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and West Bengal.

Our aim is to Promote Education One Meal at a Time by providing nutritious, wholesome, hygienic meals prepared in hi-tech kitchens which not only nourish the body but also nurture the soul.

owner_posts.post_text:
Six months. One mission. A lot of quiet, hard work.

5,700+ trees planted. 2,000+ solar lamps lighting up homes after dark. 400+ solar street lights making streets safer at night. 500+ bicycles handed out for an easier commute to school and work. 12+ classrooms rebuilt for kids who deserve better walls to learn in. One ambulance now saving lives every single day. 35+ people out of their cars for our first-ever zero emission ride.

This is what showing up, again and again, actually looks like.

First half of the year, done. Second half, let's go.

We're proud to share that 35+ members of the ThoughtSpot team came together to be part of this school beautification initiative, bringing colour and care to the school's walls.
Our heartfelt gratitude to every volunteer who gave their time and energy, and to the school for welcoming us so warmly throughout the day.

Being part of this experience meant a great deal to us, and we're thankful for the opportunity to contribute to a space where children learn and grow.

They came to colour a school's walls. Somewhere between the first brushstroke and the last, they found their own inner child again.

Grateful to the @thoughtspot volunteers who showed up with full hearts and paint-covered hands.

Turns out some "work days" don't feel like work at all.

Today the world remembers the environment. We never forgot.

Marpu doesn't live for one green day a year. Every day, every hour, our volunteers choose the planet first.

They ask for nothing back, and that is exactly what makes them the gift this earth keeps unwrapping.

The environment doesn't need a date on the calendar. It needs people who stayed.

🌱

Light for a Sustainable Future.

A reminder that 2026 is also the International Year of Volunteers for
Sustainable Development.

Both ideas anchor the same truth. Communities don't change because of
funding alone. They change because of the people who show up,
year after year, with curiosity and care.

Marpu Foundation. 23+ states. 250+ corporate partners. Over a million
volunteers and counting.

This isn't a CSR checkbox. It's what it looks like when companies actually show up.

Every frame is an employee. Engineers planting trees. Analysts painting classrooms. Managers reviving wetlands. Coders assembling solar lamps for kids who'd never had study light.
250+ corporate partners. A million people who decided their workday belonged to something larger.

Marpu doesn't run CSR drives. We run the kind your team will still talk about in the Monday standup.

Want yours in the next reel? Let's talk →

Every breath matters clean air is essential for a healthy life.

This World Asthma Day, let’s raise awareness about how pollution affects respiratory health.

A cleaner environment means fewer struggles for those living with asthma.

Small actions like reducing pollution and planting trees can create lasting impact.

Join Marpu Foundation in building a future where everyone can breathe freely. 🌿

Seed balls are one of the simplest reforestation tools, and one of the oldest.

What is a seed ball?

→ A small ball of clay, compost, and native seeds
→ Scattered across degraded land
→ Breaks open with the first rain, and the seedling grows

Why does it work?

→ Native seeds match the local ecosystem
→ The clay shell protects from birds, ants, and harsh sun
→ The compost feeds the seedling through its first weeks
→ Reaches land that conventional plantation cannot

Why does it count under CSR?

→ Aligned with Schedule VII activity 4: environmental sustainability and conservation of natural resources
→ Feeds directly into BRSR Core biodiversity disclosure
→ Hands-on, trackable, and CSR-2 documentation ready

Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals:

→ SDG 13: Climate Action
→ SDG 15: Life on Land
→ SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals

To organise a seed ball session for your team, school, or community, write to connect@marpu.org or visit

One book can spark a question. 
One question can start a journey. 
One journey can change a generation.

In underserved schools across India, children sit in classrooms with no books, no libraries, no windows to the world beyond their walls.

A single book can open that window.
This World Book Day, let's bring the gift of reading to those who need it most.

💬 Drop in the comments which book changed your life?
👉 connect@marpu.org

The biggest challenges of our time climate change, poverty, gender inequality won't be solved by bigger CSR budgets. They'll be solved by better questions.

At Marpu Foundation, one of India's largest volunteer-led NGOs across 23+ states with 250+ corporate CSR partners, social innovation starts with the people closest to the problem.



The programmes that last aren't the most expensive they're the ones built with communities, not just for them.

That's the creativity this UN observance calls for. That's the innovation sustainable development demands.



🌱 Build CSR that actually works. Partner with us at marpu.org

name: CRY - Child Rights and You | NGO in Mumbai
description:
Child Rights and You (CRY) is an Indian NGO that works towards ensuring the rights of underprivileged children in India. We have been working to ensure education, health, nutrition and safety of India's children since 1979 and have impacted over 4.7 million children.

CRY works with project partners at the grassroots level to create sustainable change for India’s children.

owner.name: CRY - Child Rights and You | NGO in Mumbai (Owner)

owner_posts.post_text:
67% of young children in India are quietly fighting a battle you can’t see.

Anaemia can limit a child’s ability to stay active, learn, and grow with confidence, often starting early and going unnoticed.

At CRY, we work with communities to change this by improving access to nutritious food, building awareness around child health, and supporting regular health check-ups, so children can grow stronger every day.

Source: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (based on NFHS-5 data)

Read more by clicking on the link below

Every child deserves a safe childhood — a chance to learn, play, and grow without fear. The Protection of Child Rights Act and related laws aim to ensure every child in India grows up safe and educated. However, in 2025–2026 many children still face abuse, neglect, and exploitation despite legal safeguards.

What is the Protection of Child Rights Act in India?
The Protection of Child Rights Act 2005, also known as the Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act 2005, led to the establishment of the National and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR and SCPCRs) frameworks, which monitor and safeguard child rights. Together with laws like POCSO and the Juvenile Justice Act, it protects children from abuse, labour, and discrimination.

Read more by clicking on the link below

National Science Day 2026 arrives at a crucial moment as India advances towards Viksit Bharat 2047. Strengthening scientific temper, innovation, and inclusive STEM education is essential to prepare future-ready citizens. This day is not just commemorative, it is transformative for India’s education and research ecosystem.

About National Science Day and Its Significance
What is National Science Day? – The History and Importance of the Day
About National Science Day, it is one of India’s most important science celebrations aimed at promoting scientific thinking and innovation. Initiated in 1987, National Science Day in India highlights how science improves everyday life and drives national development through research, education, and technology adoption.

Education is crucial for child development, yet a significant divide exists between urban and rural areas in India. Urban children benefit from superior infrastructure and resources, while rural counterparts often lack access to quality education. Digital classrooms are emerging as a transformative solution to bridge this gap, providing equal learning opportunities through technology. They incorporate various digital tools for more engaging and effective teaching, benefiting students by enhancing their understanding and motivation. However, challenges such as poor connectivity and limited resources hinder implementation. Collaborative efforts from governments, NGOs, and private sectors are essential to successfully scale digital education solutions, as demonstrated by organizations like CRY India, which supports the integration of digital tools in rural schools for improved learning outcomes.

featured_reviews.name: Khyati Shahh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I reached out to Poornima a few months ago for volunteering opportunities and she told me about the orientation. I was traveling to India for a couple months so I wanted to interact with kids and give back. She spoke to me about a project called Katha since I wouldn't be here for more than 2 months and then I could do online projects. I am traveling for a week in December and one more day I am committed which I told I will adjust and get back to her. Monday and Friday are the two days they need volunteers for for this project. I never had any NGO reject a volunteers help for not being there for a week. The way she was communicating, it felt like volunteers can either travel or volunteer but can't do both. Never ever seen an NGO reject someone's help. You can assign as many people as you want since someone can't commit 100 % of the days, but you rejecting someone's help sounds very weird to me atleast. Are you really going to assign her another project like you said when she is here only for 2 months? Mention any requirements you have in your initial email so volunteers can look for NGOs that fit their schedule and requirements. I was so excited and now I am disappointed, have to look for a new NGO, and a child has to wait till I can find someone who will accept my services.
One thing I definitely learnt here without volunteering is don't be too open and honest about your schedule else you won't get opportunities to help. I am sure that could be one of the reasons many volunteers commit and then leave. If God has made an arrangement, accept it and he will work things out for you.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for sharing this with us. We’re sorry to hear about the bad experience you had. Unfortunately, CRY does not offer really short stints/ few days of volunteering as we believe that to make a difference, you have to invest some dedicated time. As per our Child Protection Policy norms, we cannot expose children to new people without them committing to be with our children for a certain time as we provide our volunteers with due exposure and training to work sensitively!

name: Swades Foundation | Rural Empowerment
description: Swades Foundation, One of the Top NGOS in India working for rural empowerment. It works in four main areas of development which are Water & Sanitation, Health, Education and Livelihoods. This includes providing each home with access to a drinking water tap inside the house, an individual toilet, making primary healthcare accessible to the villagers, providing scholarships and faculties for school infrastructure, livelihood opportunities etc. In the year 2022, Swades Foundation has completed 75 dream villages project. A village qualifies as a Swades Dream Village by achieving over 40 parameters bucketed into 5 S's : Swachh(Clean),Sundar(Beautiful),Swasthya(Access to Healthcare),Sakshar(Educated) and Saksham(Self-Reliant)

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Yagnik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been immensely impressed by the Swades Foundation's work and their unwavering commitment to making a real difference in rural and tribal communities. Their work is not just genuine, but it's transformative. The impact they've had on the lives of those in need is nothing short of remarkable.

What sets Swades Foundation apart is their laser-focused goal – improving the lives of those living in underserved areas. This clarity of purpose ensures that every initiative, every project is meticulously designed to address the most pressing issues faced by these communities, be it Drinking water, sanitation, education, healthcare, or livelihood opportunities.

One of the standout features of Swades Foundation is their enthusiastic and dedicated team and management. Their passion for the cause is palpable, and it reflects in the results they achieve. They don't just implement projects; they invest in the empowerment of the people they serve.

In summary, Swades Foundation is a shining example of an organization that not only talks the talk but walks the walk. They are creating tangible, life-changing impacts, and their commitment to their mission is truly inspiring. This is the kind of organization that makes the world a better place, one rural and tribal life at a time. Kudos to the Swades Foundation!
